trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Vinefolk are flexible, creeping humanoids formed of twisting vines and leaves. They're wiry and resilient, able to lash out with their tendrils or cling to surfaces like ivy.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 20 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Vinefolk Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Lianor, Thryven, Veydra, Ivyric, Bramblek

Family Names: Greenbark, Leafstride, Thornwhisper, Vineheart, Mossbranch

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 70-100 years, withered vines signaling the end.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You don't need to eat food, but you require 4 hours of sunlight or water each day.

trait.name: Tendril Lash
trait.text: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage and have a reach of 10 feet.

trait.name: Entangling Grasp
trait.text: Once per short rest, you can attempt to restrain a creature within 10 feet. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be restrained until the start of your next turn.

trait.name: Photosynthesis
trait.text: While in direct sunlight, you regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus when you finish a short rest.

trait.name: Verdant Climber
trait.text: You have advantage on Athletics checks made to climb.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Cactoids are hardy desert survivors with spiny bodies that store water. Their sharp exteriors make them dangerous to touch, and they can survive where few others can.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 20 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Cactoid Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Pricklet, Spinar, Thornik, Saguro, Needlebit

Family Names: Sunspine, Desertroot, Cactar, Thornbranch, Sandbloom

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Up to 250 years, thickening and growing more spines with age.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You can go twice as long without food or water before suffering exhaustion.

trait.name: Spiny Defense
trait.text: When a creature hits you with an unarmed strike or grapple, it takes 1d4 piercing damage.

trait.name: Needle Spray
trait.text: Once per long rest, as an action, you can unleash a burst of spines in a 15-foot cone. Creatures must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier), taking 2d6 piercing damage on a failed save, or half on a success.

trait.name: Heat Adapted
trait.text: You have resistance to fire damage.

trait.name: Sand Strider
trait.text: You ignore movement penalties from difficult terrain made of sand.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Terran.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Lotusfolk are serene, water-rooted humanoids with blossoms that shift color with their moods. They're calm, meditative beings often tied to rivers and lakes.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 21 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Lotusfolk Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Lirien, Azura, Saphiel, Mariv, Nelora

Family Names: Waterbloom, Lotuswhisper, Petalstride, Riverheart, Bloomveil

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 120-150 years, blooming throughout their lives.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet. You also have a swimming speed of 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You require submersion in water or 4 hours of sunlight daily.

trait.name: Blooming Aura
trait.text: As a bonus action, you can emit calming pollen in a 10-foot radius. Creatures of your choice must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. Uses equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

trait.name: Tranquil Mind
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.

trait.name: Aquatic Grace
trait.text: You can breathe both air and water.

trait.name: Water Step
trait.text: You can move across the surface of calm water for up to 10 feet per turn.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Aquan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Bramblefolk are wild, barbed plantfolk made of thorny vines and tangled growth. They are fierce and chaotic, with bodies that make them both dangerous and hard to restrain.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 21 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Bramblefolk Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Thrynn, Briaric, Veyra, Sylth, Lyrven

Family Names: Thornveil, Brambleheart, Vinewrath, Prickleroot, Spikethorn

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: About 100 years, constantly regrowing thorny layers.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You don't need to eat food, but you must take in water and sunlight each day.

trait.name: Thorned Body
trait.text: When a creature within 5 feet hits you with a melee attack, it takes piercing damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Bramble Snare
trait.text: As an action, once per short rest, you can cause thorny vines to erupt in a 10-foot radius centered on you. Creatures must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be restrained until the start of your next turn.

trait.name: Wild Growth
trait.text: You know the thorn whip cantrip. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for it.

trait.name: Overgrowth Walker
trait.text: You can move through nonmagical plants and underbrush without expending extra movement.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Florans are humanoids tied to the seasons, shifting in appearance from withered bark in winter, to colorful flowered bloom in summer.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 22 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Floran Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Liora, Thalwyn, Fynara, Braelis, Sylphie

Family Names: Bloomveil, Petalstride, Sunbark, Leafwhisper, Flowerwind

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Charisma score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 80-100 years, becoming larger with age.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You don't need to eat food, but you must receive 4 hours of sunlight daily.

trait.name: Petal Charm
trait.text: You can cast charm person once per long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Fragrant Bloom
trait.text: Allies within 10 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against poison.

trait.name: Colorful Resilience
trait.text: You have resistance to poison damage.

trait.name: Season's Blessing
trait.text:
At dawn, roll a d4 to gain one of the following until the next morning:

	• (1) Advantage on Persuasion
	• (2) Resistance to cold
	• (3) Advantage on Stealth in foliage
	• (4) Extra 1d4 radiant damage on first hit each combat

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Petalborn are delicate beings made of soft petals and stems. They embody fragility but also beauty, carrying the essence of meadows and spring.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 22 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Petalborn Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Liriel, Fynna, Sylvra, Maribelle, Thalyn

Family Names: Bloomveil, Petalwhisper, Meadowstride, Sunpetal, Leafbreeze

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Charisma score increases by 2, and your Dexterity score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 50-70 years, fading like blossoms at season's end.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Small.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You require 4 hours of sunlight each day.

trait.name: Soft Step
trait.text: You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to move silently through natural terrain.

trait.name: Petal Dance
trait.text: As a reaction, when targeted by an attack, you can impose disadvantage on the attack roll by scattering petals in a dazzling display. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier per long rest.

trait.name: Bloom Burst
trait.text: You know the druidcraft cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Gentle Presence
trait.text: You have advantage on Animal Handling checks.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Briarfolk are dense, bark-covered plantfolk with protective thorns and heavy growth. They embody resilience, standing as living bulwarks in forests and wildlands. Briarfolk are known as a cheerful and mischievous lot, usually found pulling pranks on travelers or putting together elaborate traps in the forest.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 23 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Briarfolk Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Tharven, Brial, Klyric, Sylbor, Veyth

Family Names: Barkshield, Thornroot, Rootbark, Brambleveil, Woodstride

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 200 years, growing more barklike with age.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You do not need to eat, but you must absorb water and sunlight daily.

trait.name: Natural Armor
trait.text: Your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier when not wearing armor.

trait.name: Thorned Bulk
trait.text: When you successfully grapple a creature, it takes piercing damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Rooted Fortitude
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being pushed or knocked prone.

trait.name: Earthen Step
trait.text: You ignore difficult terrain made of natural earth or roots.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Willowen are ethereal, glowing plantfolk resembling flowing willows or ghostly vines. They are serene and haunting, and each is a child of an ancient "Home Tree", to which their life essence is tied to. They live so long as their Home Tree does, and are able to be reborn through this connection.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 23 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Willowen Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Sylvara, Liorael, Thalwen, Veylira, Nyssara

Family Names: Ghostbough, Veilbranch, Lumewillow, Wisprune, Moonroot

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Dexterity score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Potentially eternal if their trees survive.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet. You can also hover 5 feet above the ground.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You do not eat or drink, but you must spend 4 hours rooted in meditation each day.

trait.name: Luminous Veil
trait.text: You can shed dim light in a 20-foot radius or extinguish it at will.

trait.name: Drifting Step
trait.text: Once per short rest, you can teleport up to 30 feet to a space you can see.

trait.name: Ghostly Regrowth
trait.text: When reduced to 0 hit points, you can instead become dormant wisps, reforming at the base of your home tree within 1d4 hours. This can occur only once per long rest.

trait.name: Willow's Grace
trait.text: You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects you can see.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Sapbloods are crystalline humanoids made of living amber and resin. Slow but resilient, they often carry preserved memories of ancient forests within their translucent forms.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 24 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Sapblood Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Auric, Sylbera, Rilith, Thamiel, Velmara

Family Names: Amberveil, Resinroot, Sunbark, Goldenbough, Treeglass

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Effectively immortal unless shattered.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You do not need to eat or drink, but you must root in soil for 1 hour each day.

trait.name: Hardened Resin
trait.text: You have resistance to poison damage, and you cannot be paralyzed.

trait.name: Sticky Grip
trait.text: You have advantage on checks to grapple, and creatures have disadvantage to escape your grapple.

trait.name: Amber Stasis
trait.text: When reduced to 0 HP, you may instead petrify yourself in amber until stabilized. Once per long rest.

trait.name: Crystal Memory
trait.text: You gain proficiency in History, as your form carries ancient memories within.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Primordial.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Pumpklings are animated pumpkin-headed folk, tied to harvests and festivals. They embody mischief and bounty, with hollow bodies and glowing eyes.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 24 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Pumpkling Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Patch, Lumin, Gourdik, Felvine, Thistle

Family Names: Harvestlight, Vineveil, Seedbloom, Autumnroot, Pumpbranch

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Charisma score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 80 years, unless replanted from their seeds.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You do not need to eat or drink, but you require sunlight or water for nourishment.

trait.name: Lantern Glow
trait.text: You can shed bright light in a 20-foot radius at will.

trait.name: Harvest Blessing
trait.text: Once per long rest, you can cast Goodberry without a spell slot.

trait.name: Trickster's Vine
trait.text: As a reaction, when a creature within 30 feet moves, you can attempt to trip them. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier) or fall prone.

trait.name: Autumn Resilience
trait.text: You have resistance to necrotic damage.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Sporeminds are fungal humanoids, their caps and spores forming part of their body. They are often strange, quiet, and symbiotic, with a natural connection to decay.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 25 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Sporemind Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Mycora, Fennik, Sporiel, Thallus, Lymbra

Family Names: Mushroot, Capveil, Sporeshade, Mycelbloom, Fungbranch

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 40—60 years, spreading spores at death.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Fungal Nature
trait.text: You do not need to eat food, but you must spend 1 hour each day in a damp or shaded environment.

trait.name: Spore Burst
trait.text: As an action, once per short rest, you can emit spores in a 10-foot radius. Enemies must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or be poisoned until the start of your next turn.

trait.name: Symbiotic Resilience
trait.text: You are immune to disease and have advantage on saving throws against poison.

trait.name: Fungal Link
trait.text: You can communicate simple ideas with other fungi and mycelium networks within 30 feet.

trait.name: Rot's Gift
trait.text: You know the infestation cantrip. Constitution is your spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Undercommon.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Bonsai Ancestors are miniature, wise treefolk, resembling small but ancient beings with gnarled bark and delicate leaves. Though small, they are deeply rooted in tradition and magic.

Source:	Grand Species Almanac v1.1 p. 25 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Bonsai Ancestor Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Kiyori, Tanuki, Lumei, Fushin, Yorin

Family Names: Leafbark, Rootweave, Tinybranch, Sungrove, Mossveil

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Intelligence score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Up to 500 years, their form growing more twisted with time.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Small.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

trait.name: Plant Nature
trait.text: You require 4 hours of still meditation under sunlight daily.

trait.name: Rooted Wisdom
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

trait.name: Bonsai Fortitude
trait.text: When you take the Dodge action, you can root yourself, gaining temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus until the start of your next turn.

trait.name: Ancient Magic
trait.text: You know the guidance cantrip. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

trait.name: Miniature Frame
trait.text: You can move through the space of any creature larger than you, and you can use cover one size smaller than usual.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Sylvan.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Born from snowdrifts and frozen mists, Frostlings are glittering sprites of winter. Their tiny bodies shimmer with crystalline ice, and their touch carries the sting of frost.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 27 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Frostling Names
trait.text: Given Names: Nibblenip, Snowscrap, Chillip, Aurellin, Frostarin, Shiverclaw, Rimebite, Frostlash, Iselune, Frostiwick, Hrimlek

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: 30-50 years, until you fade into frost and snow.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Tiny.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 20 feet.

trait.name: Elemental Nature
trait.text: You don't need to eat or drink, but you must rest. Instead of sleeping, you enter a 4-hour trance.

trait.name: Tiny Trickster
trait.text: You cannot wield heavy weapons or wear heavy armor. You can pass through a space as narrow as 6 inches wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Frozen Touch
trait.text: You know the ray of frost cantrip. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for it.

trait.name: Snow Camouflage
trait.text: You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in snowy or icy terrain.

trait.name: Chilling Aura
trait.text: As a bonus action, you can emit a brief aura of frost. Each creature of your choice within 5 feet must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or have its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

trait.name: Cold Resistance
trait.text: You have resistance to cold damage.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Primordial.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Born of sparks and campfire embers, Emberlings are flickering sprites of flame. Their tiny bodies glow with a faint orange light, and they leave trails of ash and warmth wherever they go.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 27 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Kindle Spark

trait.name: Fire Resistance

trait.name: Description

trait.name: Description

Crystalits are glittering sprites born from gemstones and crystalline caverns. Their bodies sparkle with refracted light, and their voices hum like resonant chimes.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Tiny.

trait.name: Speed

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Orcs trace their creation to the one-eyed god Gruumsh, an unstoppable warrior and powerful leader. The divine qualities of Gruumsh resonate within orcs, granting them a reflection of his toughness and tenacity that can't be matched, and the god equipped his children to be able to live above or below ground.
	On some worlds, such as Eberron, orcs were among the first defenders of the natural order from the encroachments of Fiends and other extraplanar threats. Gruumsh's blessings have made orcs tireless guardians and mighty allies wherever they are found, even when they turn their devotion to other gods.

Landrider Orcs are guardians of the open plains, known for their harmony with the land and their kinship with beasts. They are strong yet steady, their lives measured by the rhythm of the herds they guide and the bonds of family and community they cherish.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Kingdoms rich in ancient grandeur, halls carved into the roots of mountains, the echoing of picks and hammers in deep mines and blazing forges, a commitment to clan and tradition, and a burning hatred of goblins and orcs-these common threads unite all dwarves.

Mesa Dwarves carve their homes into towering cliffs and sun-bleached plateaus, blending ingenuity with reverence for the harsh beauty around them. They quarry stone from canyon walls, craft water-saving cisterns, and use reflective mirrors to channel sunlight into their subterranean halls.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 40 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Short and Stout
trait.text:
Bold and hardy, dwarves are known as skilled warriors, miners, and workers of stone and metal. Though they stand well under 5 feet tall, dwarves are so broad and compact that they can weigh as much as a human standing nearly two feet taller. Their courage and endurance are also easily a match for any of the larger folk.
	Dwarven skin ranges from deep brown to a paler hue tinged with red, but the most common shades are light brown or deep tan, like certain tones of earth.
	Their hair, worn long but in simple styles, is usually black, gray, or brown, though paler dwarves often have red hair. Male dwarves value their beards highly and groom them carefully.

trait.name: Long Memory, Long Grudges
trait.text:
Dwarves can live to be more than 400 years old, so the oldest living dwarves often remember a very different world. For example, some of the oldest dwarves living in Citadel Felbarr (in the world of the Forgotten Realms) can recall the day, more than three centuries ago, when orcs conquered the fortress and drove them into an exile that lasted over 250 years. This longevity grants them a perspective on the world that shorter-lived races such as humans and halflings lack.
	Dwarves are solid and enduring like the mountains they love, weathering the passage of centuries with stoic endurance and little change. They respect the traditions of their clans, tracing their ancestry back to the founding of their most ancient strongholds in the youth of the world, and don't abandon those traditions lightly. Part of those traditions is devotion to the gods of the dwarves, who uphold the dwarven ideals of industrious labor, skill in battle, and devotion to the forge.
	Individual dwarves are determined and loyal, true to their word and decisive in action, sometimes to the point of stubbornness. Many dwarves have a strong sense of justice, and they are slow to forget wrongs they have suffered. A wrong done to one dwarf is a wrong done to the dwarf's entire clan, so what begins as one dwarf's hunt for vengeance can become a full-blown clan feud.

trait.name: Clans and Kingdoms
trait.text:
Dwarven kingdoms stretch deep beneath the mountains where the dwarves mine gems and precious metals and forge items of wonder. They love the beauty and artistry of precious metals and fine jewelry, and in some dwarves this love festers into avarice. Whatever wealth they can't find in their mountains, they gain through trade. They dislike boats, so enterprising humans and halflings frequently handle trade in dwarven goods along water routes. Trustworthy members of other races are welcome in dwarf settlements, though some areas are off limits even to them.
	The chief unit of dwarven society is the clan, and dwarves highly value social standing. Even dwarves who live far from their own kingdoms cherish their clan identities and affiliations, recognize related dwarves, and invoke their ancestors' names in oaths and curses. To be clanless is the worst fate that can befall a dwarf.
	Dwarves in other lands are typically artisans, especially weaponsmiths, armorers, and jewelers. Some become mercenaries or bodyguards, highly sought after for their courage and loyalty.

trait.name: Gods, Gold, and Clan
trait.text: Dwarves who take up the adventuring life might be motivated by a desire for treasure-for its own sake, for a specific purpose, or even out of an altruistic desire to help others. Other dwarves are driven by the command or inspiration of a deity, a direct calling or simply a desire to bring glory to one of the dwarf gods. Clan and ancestry are also important motivators. A dwarf might seek to restore a clan's lost honor, avenge an ancient wrong the clan suffered, or earn a new place within the clan after having been exiled. Or a dwarf might search for the axe wielded by a mighty ancestor, lost on the field of battle centuries ago.

trait.name: Slow to Trust
trait.text:
Dwarves get along passably well with most other races. "The difference between an acquaintance and a friend is about a hundred years," is a dwarf saying that might be hyperbole, but certainly points to how difficult it can be for a member of a short-lived race like humans to earn a dwarf's trust.

	Elves. "It's not wise to depend on the elves. No telling what an elf will do next; when the hammer meets the orc's head, they're as apt to start singing as to pull out a sword. They're flighty and frivolous. Two things to be said for them, though: They don't have many smiths, but the ones they have do very fine work. And when orcs or goblins come streaming down out of the mountains, an elf's good to have at your back. Not as good as a dwarf, maybe, but no doubt they hate the orcs as much as we do."

	Halflings. "Sure, they're pleasant folk. But show me a halfling hero. An empire, a triumphant army. Even a treasure for the ages made by halfling hands. Nothing. How can you take them seriously?"

	Humans. "You take the time to get to know a human, and by then the human's on her deathbed. If you're lucky, she's got kin-a daughter or granddaughter, maybe-who's got hands and heart as good as hers. That's when you can make a human friend. And watch them go!. They set their hearts on something, they'll get it whether it's a dragon's hoard or an empire's throne. You have to admire that kind of dedication, even if it gets them in trouble more often than not."

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
A constant hum of busy activity pervades the warrens and neighborhoods where gnomes form their close-knit communities. Louder sounds punctuate the hum: a crunch of grinding gears here, a minor explosion there, a yelp of surprise or triumph, and especially bursts of laughter. Gnomes take delight in life, enjoying every moment of invention, exploration, investigation, creation, and play.

High in the jungle, Canopy Gnomes weave rope bridges, wind-spun platforms, and leafy homes. They are keen observers of plants and wildlife, blending clever engineering with an instinctive sense of balance. Their villages ring with laughter, birdsong, and the creak of branches swaying in the breeze. Mischief and curiosity are prized, yet they honor the rhythms of the forest, crafting remedies, dyes, and tools from the bounty of the green world.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 41 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Vibrant Expression
trait.text:
A gnome's energy and enthusiasm for living shines through every inch his or her tiny body. Gnomes average slightly over 3 feet tall and weigh 40 to 45 pounds. Their tan or brown faces are usually adorned with broad smiles (beneath their prodigious noses), and their bright eyes shine with excitement. Their fair hair has a tendency to stick out in every direction, as if expressing the gnome's insatiable interest in everything around.
	A gnome's personality is writ large in his or her appearance. A male gnome's beard, in contrast to his wild hair, is kept carefully trimmed but often styled into curious forks or neat points. A gnome's clothing, though usually made in modest earth tones, is elaborately decorated with embroidery, embossing, or gleaming jewels.

trait.name: Delighted Dedication
trait.text:
As far as gnomes are concerned, being alive is a wonderful thing, and they squeeze every ounce of enjoyment out of their three to five centuries of life. Humans might wonder about getting bored over the course of such a long life, and elves take plenty of time to savor the beauties of the world in their long years, but gnomes seem to worry that even with all that time, they can't get in enough of the things they want to do and see.
	Gnomes speak as if they can't get the thoughts out of their heads fast enough. Even as they offer ideas and opinions on a range of subjects, they manage to listen carefully to others, adding the appropriate exclamations of surprise and appreciation along the way.
	Though gnomes love jokes of all kinds, particularly puns and pranks, they're just as dedicated to the more serious tasks they undertake. Many gnomes are skilled engineers, alchemists, tinkerers, and inventors. They're willing to make mistakes and laugh at themselves in the process of perfecting what they do, taking bold (sometimes foolhardy) risks and dreaming large.

trait.name: Bright Burrows
trait.text:
Gnomes makes their homes in hilly, wooded lands. They live underground but get more fresh air than dwarves do, enjoying the natural, living world on the surface where ever they can. Their homes are well hidden by both clever construction and simple illusions. Welcome visitors are quickly ushered into the bright, warm burrows. Those who are not welcome are unlikely to find the burrows in the first place.
	Gnomes who settle in human lands are commonly gemcutters, engineers, sages, or tinkerers. Some human families retained gnome tutors, ensuring that their pupils enjoy a mix of serious learning and delighted enjoyment. A gnome might tutor several generations of a single human family over the course of his or her long life.

trait.text: Curious and impulsive, gnomes might take up adventuring as a way to see the world or for the love of exploring. As lovers of gems and other fine items, some gnomes take to adventuring as s quick, if dangerous, path to wealth. Regardless of what spurs them to adventure, gnomes who adopt this way of life eke as much enjoyment out of it as they do out of any other activity they undertake, sometimes to the great annoyance of their adventuring companions.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Whether descended from a celestial being or infused with heavenly power, aasimar are mortals who carry a spark of the Upper Planes within their souls. They can fan that spark to bring light, ease wounds, and unleash the fury of the heavens.
	Aasimar can arise among any population of mortals. They resemble their parents, but they live for up to 160 years and often have features that hint at their celestial heritage. These often begin subtle and become more obvious when the aasimar gains the ability to reveal their full celestial nature. The Aasimar Celestial Features table has examples you can choose or use as inspiration to create your own.

Aasimar Celestial Features:
d6 | Celestial Feature
1 | A dusting of metallic, white, or charcoal freckles
2 | Metallic, luminous, or dark eyes
3 | Starkly colored hair
4 | An unusual hue tinting your shadow
5 | A ghostly halo crowning your head
6 | Rainbows gleaming on your skin

Luminants are swift heralds and guardians, often serving gods of light, freedom, or travel. Their skin may shimmer faintly, and their eyes gleam like dawnlight.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Elves are a magical people of otherworldly grace, living in the world but not entirely part of it. They live in places of ethereal beauty, in the midst of ancient forests or in silvery spires glittering with faerie light, where soft music drifts through the air and gentle fragrances waft on the breeze. Elves love nature and magic, art and artistry, music and poetry, and the good things of the world.

Highpeak Elves dwell in eyries carved from cliffs or in sprawling stone halls hidden among snow-capped ridges. Their lives blend quiet contemplation with agile hunts along treacherous slopes. They value endurance, patience, and the beauty of stark horizons.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 42 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Slender and Graceful
trait.text:
With their unearthly grace and fine features, elves appear hauntingly beautiful to humans and members of many other races. They are slightly shorter than humans on average, ranging from well under 5 feet tall to just over 6 feet. They are more slender than humans, weighing only 100 to 145 pounds. Males and females are about the same height, and males are only marginally heavier than females.
	Elves' coloration encompasses the normal human range and also includes skin in shades of copper, bronze, and almost bluish-white, hair of green or blue, and eyes like pools of liquid gold or silver. Elves have no facial and little body hair. They favor elegant clothing in bright colors, and they enjoy simple yet lovely jewelry.

trait.name: A Timeless Perspective
trait.text:
Elves can live well over 700 years, giving them a broad perspective on events that might trouble the shorterlived races more deeply. They are more often amused than excited, and more likely to be curious than greedy. They tend to remain aloof and unfazed by petty happenstance. When pursuing a goal, however, whether adventuring on a mission or learning a new skill or art, elves can be focused and relentless. They are slow to make friends and enemies, and even slower to forget them. They reply to petty insults with disdain and to serious insults with vengeance.
	Like the branches of a young tree, elves are flexible in the face of danger. They trust in diplomacy and compromise to resolve differences before they escalate to violence. They have been known to retreat from intrusions into their woodland homes, confident that they can simply wait the invaders out. But when the need arises, elves reveal a stern martial side, demonstrating skill with sword, bow, and strategy.

trait.name: Hidden Woodland Realms
trait.text:
Most elves dwell in small forest villages hidden among the trees. Elves hunt game, gather food, and grow vegetables, and their skill and magic allow them to support themselves without the need for clearing and plowing land. They are talented artisans, crafting finely worked clothes and art objects. Their contact with outsiders is usually limited, though a few elves make a good living by trading crafted items for metals (which they have no interest in mining).
	Elves encountered outside their own lands are commonly traveling minstrels, artists, or sages. Human nobles compete for the services of elf instructors to teach swordplay or magic to their children.

trait.name: Exploration and Adventure
trait.text: Elves take up adventuring out of wanderlust. Since they are so long-lived, they can enjoy centuries of exploration and discovery. They dislike the pace of human society, which is regimented from day to day but constantly changing over decades, so they find careers that let them travel freely and set their own pace. Elves also enjoy exercising their martial prowess or gaining greater magical power, and adventuring allows them to do so. Some might join with rebels fighting against oppression, and others might become champions of moral causes.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Grungs are aggressive froglike humanoids found in rain forests and tropical jungles. They are fiercely territorial and see themselves as superior to most other creatures.
	Grung society is a caste system. Each caste lays eggs in a separate hatching pool, and juvenile grungs join their caste upon emergence from the hatchery. All grungs are a dull greenish gray when they are born, but each individual takes on the color of its caste as it grows to adulthood. From lowest to highest caste, grungs can be green, blue, purple, red, orange, or gold.
	All grungs secrete a substance that is harmless to them but poisonous to other creatures. A grung also uses venom to poison its weapons. Grungs are always on the lookout for creatures they can capture and enslave. Grungs use slaves for all manner of menial tasks, but mostly they just like bossing them around. Slaves are fed mildly poisoned food to keep them lethargic and compliant. A creature afflicted in this way over a long period of time becomes a shell of its former self and can be restored to normalcy only by magic. Being amphibious, grungs require water to live; any grung that fails to immerse itself in water for at least 1 hour during a day becomes quite exhausted.
	Green grungs are the tribe's warriors, hunters, and laborers, and blue grungs work as artisans and in other domestic roles. Supervising and guiding both groups are the purple grungs, which serve as administrators and commanders. Red grungs are the tribe's scholars and magic users. They are superior to purple, blue, and green grungs and given proper respect even by grungs of higher status. Higher castes include orange grungs, which are elite warriors that have authority over all lesser grungs, and gold grungs, which hold the highest leadership positions. A tribe's sovereign is always a gold grung.
	A grung normally remains in its caste for life. On rare occasions, an individual that distinguishes itself with great deeds can earn an invitation to join a higher caste. Through a combination of herbal tonics and ritual magic, an elevated grung changes color and is inducted into its new caste in the same way that a juvenile of the caste would be. From then on, the grung and its progeny are members of the higher caste.

Frost Grungs make their homes in half-frozen marshes, icy caves, or hollowed-out snowbanks. Their skin often bears pale blues, grays, or muted whites with subtle iridescence, allowing them to vanish into snowfields. Their tribes cultivate mosses and hardy pondweeds beneath ice-crusted pools and hunt fish, hares, and seabirds.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 42 (Homebrew)

Tribal Names: Icewhisper, Frostcoil, Snowmantle, Coldrib, Glacertide, Shardback, Hailflood

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Frost Grungs reach maturity within a year of hatching and rarely live beyond 50 years.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Grungs stand between 2½ and 3½ feet tall and average about 30 pounds. Your size is Small.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: You can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Poisonous Skin
trait.text: Any creature that grapples you or otherwise touches your skin with bare skin must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or be poisoned for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

trait.name: Standing Leap
trait.text: Your long jump is up to 25 feet and your high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

trait.name: Water Dependency
trait.text: You must immerse yourself in water or icy slush for at least 1 hour per day, or you suffer one level of exhaustion at the end of the day.

trait.name: Cold-Blooded Endurance
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against extreme cold and resistance to cold damage.

trait.name: Frost-Slick Skin
trait.text: You secrete a thin, frost-resistant film that protects you from ice-burn and allows you to slip through snow or frozen terrain. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws to resist being grappled or restrained.

trait.name: Tundra Camouflage
trait.text: You can take the Hide action as a bonus action when you are lightly obscured by snow, ice, or rocky tundra.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Grung and Common.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
A subterranean folk, goblins can be found in every corner of the multiverse, often beside their bugbear and hobgoblin kin. Long before the god Maglubiyet conquered them, early goblins served in the court of the Queen of Air and Darkness, one of the Feywild's archfey. Goblins thrived in her dangerous domain thanks to a special boon from her—a supernatural knack for finding the weak spots in foes larger than themselves and for getting out of trouble. Goblins brought this fey boon with them to worlds across the Material Plane, even if they don't remember the fey realm they inhabited before Maglubiyet's rise. Now many goblins pursue their own destinies, escaping the plots of both archfey and gods.

Gloom Goblins dwell in tight-knit warrens carved into cavern walls, lit by glowing fungi and gemstone shards. Resourceful and sharp-eyed, they thrive by hunting blind cave lizards, mining rare crystals, or trading scavenged goods with drow and duergar. Their tribes rely on stealth, speed, and cooperation, weaving through stalagmites and shadow to avoid the notice of larger predators.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 43 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Gloom Goblin Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Skiv, Nax, Drell, Vek, Zik, Trel, Fenn, Rax, Pikk, Mox

Tribal Names: Shadowhollow, Stonevein, Darkcoil, Crystalburrow, Fungalwarren, Emberroot

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Gloom Goblins mature by age 12 and rarely live past 60 years.

trait.name: Size
trait.text:
Goblins are between 3 and 4 feet tall and weigh between 40 and 80 pounds. Your size is Small.

To set your height and weight randomly, start with rolling a size modifier:

Size modifier = 2d4
Height = 3 feet + 5 inches + your size modifier in inches
Weight in pounds = 35 + your size modifier

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: You can see in dim light within 120 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of red.

trait.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
trait.text: While in direct sunlight, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

trait.name: Stone Skitter
trait.text: You have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed on rough stone or natural cavern walls.

trait.name: Cavern Ambusher
trait.text: You can take the Hide action as a bonus action while in dim light, darkness, or rocky terrain.

trait.name: Underdark Cunning
trait.text: You gain proficiency in Stealth or Survival (your choice). When traveling underground, you and up to five companions you lead can't become lost except by magical means.

trait.name: Nimble Escape
trait.text: You can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of your turns.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Goblin. Many also pick up bits of Undercommon.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Giff are tall, broad-shouldered folk with hippo-like features. Some have smooth skin, while others have short bristles on their faces and the tops of their heads. As beings of impressive size and unforgettable appearance, giff are noticed wherever they go.
	Most giff believe they originated on one world, but their home world is now the stuff of legend, because no living giff has seen it or knows where it is. The divine beings who created giff have likewise been forgotten. Their titanic petrified bodies drift on the Astral Sea, isolated and unrecognizable in their current forms.
	Although they don't realize it, giff are drawn to the Astral Plane because, on a deep psychic level, they remain connected to their creator gods, who have just enough divine spark left in them to imbue giff with sparks of their own, which giff have learned to channel through their weapons. Most giff have no idea where this so-called astral spark comes from, but they feel its presence most strongly when they are in Wildspace or the Astral Sea.
	Giff are split into two camps concerning how their name is pronounced. Half of them say it with a hard g, half with a soft g. Disagreements over the correct pronunciation often blossom into hard feelings, loud arguments, and head-butting contests, but they rarely escalate beyond that.

Spherebound Giff are practical, amiable folk who build timber lodges atop stilts or carve homes into riverbanks. They are at ease wading through reed beds, gliding along slow-moving waters in dugout canoes, or hauling nets full of fish. Many serve as guardians of their boggy homelands, protecting hidden pools, sacred groves, and the delicate balance of marsh life. Though grounded in temperament, they love lively storytelling and hearty feasts after a long day's work.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 43 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Spherebound Giff Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Borin, Haska, Talvik, Oren, Kessa, Mivar, Jorin, Sula, Fend, Ril

Family/Tribal Names: Reedstilt, Marshwalker, Bogfoot, Riverbranch, Caneweave, Fenhome

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Strength score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Giff mature around age 15 and can live up to 80 years.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Amphibious Constitution
trait.text: You can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes, and you have advantage on saving throws against disease.

trait.name: Thick-Hided
trait.text: When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 12 + your Constitution modifier. You can still use a shield and gain this benefit.

trait.name: Trample Stomp
trait.text: When you hit a creature with a melee attack on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to shove it prone. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

trait.name: Swampwise
trait.text: You gain proficiency in one of the following: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival. When traveling through swamps or jungles, you and companions you guide ignore difficult terrain caused by mud, vines, or shallow water.

trait.name: Powerful Build
trait.text: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Giff.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Born of dragons, as their name proclaims, the dragonborn walk proudly through a world that greets them with fearful incomprehension. Shaped by draconic gods or the dragons themselves, dragonborn originally hatched from dragon eggs as a unique race, combining the best attributes of dragons and humanoids. Some dragonborn are faithful servants to true dragons, others form the ranks of soldiers in great wars, and still others find themselves adrift, with no clear calling in life.

Solar dragonborn often hail from high plateaus, sunlit deserts, or observatories built atop remote mountains. Some serve as wandering champions, bringing warmth and clarity to dark places, while others form radiant clans that prize honor, curiosity, and the steady brilliance of the sun.

Source:	Fredrick's Fortunes p. 44 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Proud Dragon Kin
trait.text:
Dragonborn look very much like dragons standing erect in humanoid form, though they lack wings or a tail. The first dragonborn had scales of vibrant hues matching the colors of their dragon kin, but generations of interbreeding have created a more uniform appearance. Their small, fine scales are usually brass or bronze in color, sometimes ranging to scarlet, rust, gold, or copper-green. They are tall and strongly built, often standing close to 6½ feet tall and weighing 300 pounds or more. Their hands and feet are smiting, talonlike claws with three fingers and a thumb on each hand.
	The blood of a particular type of dragon runs very strong through some dragonborn clans. These dragonborn often boast scales that more closely match those of their dragon ancestor-bright red, green, blue, or white, lustrous black, or gleaming metallic like gold, silver, brass, copper, or bronze.

trait.name: Self-Sufficient Clans
trait.text:
To any dragonborn, the clan is more important than life itself. Dragonborn owe their devotion and respect to their clan above all else, even the gods. Each dragonborn's conduct reflects on the honor of his or her clan, and bringing dishonor to the clan can result in expulsion and exile. Each dragonborn knows his or her station and duties within the clan, and honor demands maintaining the bounds of that position.
	A continual drive for self-improvement reflects the self-sufficiency, of the race as a whole. Dragonborn value skill and excellence in all endeavors. They hate to fail, and they push themselves to extreme efforts before they give up on something. A dragonborn holds mastery of that particular skill as a lifetime goal. Members of other races who share the same commitment find it easy to earn the respect of a dragonborn.
	Though all dragonborn strive to be self-sufficient, they recognize that help is sometimes needed in difficult situations. But the best source for such help is the clan, and when a client needs help, it turns to another dragonborn clan before seeking aid from other races or even from the gods.

trait.name: Solar Dragonborn Names
trait.text:
Given Names: Solan, Raelis, Aurion, Helia, Lysar, Tharion, Veyra, Kaelen

Clan/Family Names: Sunspire, Dawnfire, Lightward, Radiantcrest, Solarwind, Brightscale

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Strength score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Solar dragonborn mature at the same rate as humans but can live to about 80 years.

trait.name: Size
trait.text:
Dragonborn are taller and heavier than humans, standing well over 6 feet tall and averaging almost 250 pounds. Your size is Medium.

To set your height and weight randomly, start with rolling a size modifier:

Size modifier = 2d8
Height = 5 feet + 6 inches + your size modifier in inches
Weight in pounds = 175 + (2d6 × your size modifier)

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

trait.name: Draconic Ancestry
trait.text: Your draconic ancestor is a Solar Dragon, a celestial wyrm that soars through light-filled voids.

trait.name: Radiant Breath
trait.text: You can unleash a blast of searing light. Each creature in a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide must make a Dexterity saving throw. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d6 on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

trait.name: Solar Resistance
trait.text: You have resistance to radiant damage.

trait.name: Lightbearer
trait.text: You know the light cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast daylight once with this trait, regaining the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
When I was a child I sought out the guardian of my people's ancestral forest. I wandered for days deep within the woods, and I am certain that I never have found the ancient gardener had he wished to remain hidden from me. His true name was too much long for me to comprehend, but he allowed me to call him Whiproot.
	For a year and a day he taught me the ways of the wood, slowly nurturing my druidic potential. Sometimes I still see those ancient green eyes in my dreams. Though I have grown old, I know that the gardener is still out there in the forest of my people, quietly singing to himself as he tends to the trees.
— Zumug, Archdruid of the North

Source:	LaserLlama's New & Alternate Player Races v2.0.0 p. 2 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Elder Gardeners
trait.text: Deep in the forests of the world dwell a forgotten people, the Entlings. They are the ancient caretakers of the forest who awoke at the dawn of the world. To many, they are creatures of myth and folktale, reclusive tree-like people with skin like bark and hair that resembles tree-tops and verdant gardens. Though these gardeners are few in number, they are very much real, though they prefer to be forgotten. Most Entlings will happily spend their exceptionally love lives tending to the large swaths of wilderness under their care, learning the names of every root, flower, and tree under their protection.

trait.name: Shepherds of the Forest
trait.text:
Entlings care deeply for the plants under their care, and often watch them grow from seedling to fully mature plants. They prefer to spend their lives in quiet harmony with nature, only occasionally interacting with other mortals. They carefully maintain the natural order of the ecosystems they dwell in, culling creatures that grow to numerous, nurturing those on the brink of extinction, and all the relationships in between.
	Though rarely roused to action, Entlings who strike out into the world often do so to protect the forests under their protection. Though slow to anger, their fury knows no bounds when evil or blight threatens the groves that they have raised from seedlings. Entlings who leave the forest usually find it difficult to fit in amongst civilized settlements, and usually struggle to understand the norms and customs of normal folk. Entlings who become adventurers most often train to defend the wild as a ranger or join a local Circle of druids.

trait.name: Entling Names
trait.text: Due to their long lifespans and relaxed disposition, Entling names are often exceptionally detailed stories that can take days to explain. Often, the Entlings that interact with mortals will adopt the name of their favorite plant, tree, or flower.

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Entlings are considered to be adults around the age of 100, and can live to be over 1000 years old if they spend their lives in peace. Hasty Entlings that take up the stressful live of adventuring can shorten their lifespan by up to 500 years.

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: You are both Humanoid and Plant.

trait.name: Alignment
trait.text: Entlings are a naturally peaceful folk that care for all living things, and they tend towards good alignments.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Entlings reflect the forests and plants they tend to, and thus come in all shapes and sizes. Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Gardener's Lore
trait.text: You gain proficiency in the Nature skill, and you can make a Wisdom (Nature) check whenever you would normally make an Intelligence (Nature) check.

trait.name: Natural Magic
trait.text: You know one cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

trait.name: Photosynthetic
trait.text: You don't need to eat or drink so long as you are exposed to sunlight for 1 hour each day. To gain the benefits of a long rest, you must spend at least 6 hours in an inactive, motionless state, though you remain aware of your surroundings. In this state, you can see and hear as normal, and you appear to be a normal tree unless closely inspected.

trait.name: Shepherd of the Forest
trait.text: Through sound and gestures, you may communicate simple ideas with plants of all kinds.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common, and your choice of either Druidic, Sylvan, or Elvish.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
From atop the great walls of Hammerdeep I watched as the young half-dwarf disappeared into the swamp. Based on talent along, he should have been chosen as apprentice to the master smith of the great walled city. Sadly, due to his human mother, the young smith had been passed over for a less skilled, but full-blooded dwarf.
	I always admired how he refused to stoop to the menial work delegated to half-dwarves, and I was determined to help him earn the right to use the clan name of his father. I knew the task would be dangerous, especially to a dwarf with so little experience as a warrior, but if the he could succeed in slaying the young dragon that had taken up residence in the swamp, the elders would have no choice but to accept him.
— Lord Thorin Stormfist
Hero of Hammerdeep

Source:	LaserLlama's New & Alternate Player Races v2.0.0 p. 3 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Dwarven Tradition
trait.text:
Half-dwarves often showcase the best of both of their parents' heritage. Like dwarves, they will usually place high value on honorable conduct and reputation. And, although they are not considered full members of their respective clans, most half-dwarves will go to great lengths to win acceptance, or prevent bringing shame upon the clan of their dwarven parent.
	Often, when a clan has risky or nefarious business to take care of, they will task a half-dwarf with taking care of things. That way, should things go poorly, dishonor is not brought upon a full-blooded member of the clan. Seeking to belong, half-dwarves will go to great lengths to gain the favor of their dwarven relatives. Refusing to deny their human heritage, it is very difficult, and requires great feats of service for a half-dwarf to be recognized by the elders as a member of the clan.

trait.name: Human Innovation
trait.text: From their human heritage, half-dwarves bring the spark of innovation and desire to create a personal legacy. Far more individualistic then other dwarves, their innate desire to push boundaries drives them to innovate on the craftsmanship of both dwarves and humans, often ignoring the traditions of master artisans. Due to their dedication and ingenuity, half-dwarven products are often sought after by those with an eye for quality. Unfortunately, half-dwarves are rarely accepted into dwarven guilds due to dwarven tradition and customs.

trait.name: Half-Dwarf Names
trait.text: Half-dwarves are often given dwarven first names, but either take the last name of their human parent, or adopt the name Stone. Being officially recognized as a member of their clan is seen as the highest honor to be bestowed on a half-dwarf.

trait.name: Half-Dwarves of the Multiverse
trait.text:
Half-dwarves can exist in any setting that includes both humans and dwarves. A hardy folk, they often sprout up wherever these two races meet.
	In the Dark Sun setting, half-dwarves are known as Mul, and sadly, due to their natural fortitude and stamina they are prized as gladiators and laborers.

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and one other ability score of your choice increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Half-dwarves mature at the same rate humans do and reach adulthood around the age of 20. They live much longer than humans however, often close to 200 years.

trait.name: Alignment
trait.text: Half-dwarves often share the lawful bend of their dwarven heritage, but some favor more chaotic ways of life. Most tend toward good as well, with a strong sense of fair play and a belief that everyone deserves to go wherever they please and share in the benefits of a life free from tyranny.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Half-dwarves are about the same size as humans, if a little shorter and stockier. You stand between 4 1/2 and 5 1/2 feet, and weigh around 200 pounds. Your size is medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: Thanks to your dwarven blood, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. However, you can't discern color when in darkness, only shades of gray.

trait.name: Hardy
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

trait.name: Natural Craftsman
trait.text: You gain proficiency with one set of artisan's tools of your choice. You add double your proficiency bonus to any ability check you make that uses those tools.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common, Dwarvish, and one additional language of your choice. Half-dwarves often learn the language of peoples they work with.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
When the warrior awoke, he knew something was different. The last thing he remembered was the feeling of numbness that washed over him as the acid breath of the great dragon consumed him. Almost instinctively, the warrior took stock of his surroundings he seemed to be in some sort of laboratory. Across from the table on which he lay stood a mirror, and gazing upon his reflection shook him to his core.

Arcane Magen are embodiments of raw magic, and serve as assistants in arcane research.

trait.text: While most spend their lives searching for purpose, Magen come with that purpose woven into their very being. Created by powerful mages to fulfill a specific duty, Magen physically resemble adult humanoids, but pale bluish skin and maroon eyes set them apart. Their innate magic allows them to live without the food, air, and water required by mortals, but their innate magic makes them susceptible to anti-magic effects.

trait.name: Loyal Servants
trait.text: While the typical Magen is fiercely loyal to their creator, even to death, those that become adventurers are those that have thrown off the yoke of servitude. When you create a Magen, consider why they struck out into the world. Are they seeking a purpose greater than the duty they were created for?

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Intelligence score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Magen are created to resemble adult humanoids, and they show no signs of deterioration due to age. Their upper lifespan is speculated to be around 500 years old.

trait.name: Alignment
trait.text: Magen are lawful by nature, and most often reflect the alignment of their creator, be it good or evil.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Magen are roughly the size of an adult human, ranging from five to six feet tall. Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Arcane Construct
trait.text: You can be damaged by anti-magic spells. If you are targeted by dispel magic, you take 1d6 force damage per each level of the spell slot expended to cast it. You also take 1d6 force damage each time you enter, or start your turn, within an anti-magic field (or other similar effect).

trait.name: Born of the Weave
trait.text: You have advantage on all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.

trait.name: Unusual Nature
trait.text: You do not require air, food, or drink.

trait.name: Arcane Nature
trait.text: You know one cantrip of your choice from the wizard spell list. When you reach 3rd level, you learn one 1st-level wizard spell, and when you reach 5th level, you learn one 2nd-level wizard spell. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and you can cast each spell once per long rest without expending a spell slot, after which you must expend one of your own spell slots to cast it again.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common, and one other language of your choice. Most Magen are imbued with the knowledge of a language spoken by their creator.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Every fairy I've ever met has been irritating beyond belief, and I cannot fathom why the Prince of Winter hasn't expelled the little buggers from his court completely. Sure, their small stature and tiny wings allow them to access places that I certainly couldn't, and their skill with illusion magic does come in handy more often than I'd like to admit. Actually, now that I think about it, they do seem to have their uses. Maybe I need to give these tricksters another chance.
— Sir Tumnus Longfinger
Champion of the Winter Court

Source:	LaserLlama's New & Alternate Player Races v2.0.0 p. 4 (Homebrew)

trait.name: Fleeting Fancies
trait.text: Fairies may be the most spontaneous creatures in existence, constantly moving from one interest to the next as something new or exciting catches their attention. They are curious to a fault, and love to experience new things whenever they have the chance. When a fairy puts their mind to something, they put everything they have into their pursuits. Though it may not last, the determination of a fairy knows no bounds.

trait.name: Servants of the Fey Court
trait.text:
All Fairies begin their lives in the service of one of the Courts of the Feywild, and the Archfey they serve is the closest thing many of them will have to a parent. The longer a fairy spends in the presence of an Archfey, the more they start to resemble them. Those who have spent lifetimes in the service of a Fey Court often come to resemble miniature versions of Archfey, in appearance and manner. While in the Feywild, Fairies stop maturing, both physically and emotionally, when they reach adulthood, allowing them a strange perpetual immortality.

The fairies who reject a life of unchanging servitude most often do so to become adventurers on the material plane, where they can age and develop normally. Fairy adventurers often pursue their knack for illusion magic as bards, wizards, or sorcerers, though some strike pacts and become warlocks.

trait.name: Fairy Names
trait.text: Due to their whimsical nature and ever-changing interests, Fairies will change their name spontaneously when a mood takes them. Fairies usually adopt the name of a particularly beautiful natural phenomena or powerful emotion; Aurora, Dewdrop, Sunrise, Rainbow, Joy, Serenity, or Glee.

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Fairies reach adulthood a year and a day after their birth, and do not age further in the Feywild. While in mortal realms they age normally and can live to be 100 years old.

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: You are both Humanoid and Fey.

trait.name: Alignment
trait.text: Fairies hail from the courts of many different Archfey, but they are almost universally Chaotic in alignment.

trait.name: Size
trait.text:
Fairies only stand a few inches in height, the largest of which stand almost a foot tall. Your size is Tiny.
	As a Tiny creature, you can only wield weapons that have the Light property, and you cannot wear armor or clothing unless it is specifically sized to fit a creature of your stature.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 20 feet.

trait.name: Dainty Wings
trait.text: So long as you are not wearing medium or heavy armor, you have a flying speed of 30 feet and can hover, but you cannot fly, or hover, more than 10 feet off the ground. At 5th level, this 10 foot height restriction is lifted.

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put you to sleep.

trait.name: Fey Magic
trait.text: You know the minor illusion and faerie fire spells. You can cast faerie fire without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and your choice of either Sylvan or Elvish.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Paul rivers enlisted in the town guard the day he turned sixteen. None of the villagers thought that this was a particularly good idea, but no one had the heart to turn the boy away. And after all, the village hadn't been attacked by monsters in almost ten summers. Paul trained with the rest of the guardsmen, and despite his boyish personality, he was a natural with the sword and spear. Over the next few months he grew in skill and strength, and by the following summer, Paul was able to best every warrior in the village.
	Just before harvest, a group of evil cultists descended upon the small hamlet. They stole everything of value, and burned anything that couldn't be stolen. At the town's most desperate moment, with the survivors cowered in the armory, the cult's champion issued a challenge. A duel to the death for the lives of the remaining villagers. Without saying a word, Paul drew his sword and stepped forward to defend his home.
— Berthold Cornersnatch
Traveling Bard and Storyteller

In most worlds, humans are the most numerous of the mortal races, and their grit and adaptability allow them to succeed in all but the most hostile environments. Humans can be found in almost any city, town, or hamlet. They live in large social groups, and most humans dwell in permanent settlements.
	Astute humans are those, that have spent their lives honing their mental abilities. They tend to become highly specialized experts in certain subjects, ignoring all other areas of study for the sake of mastery. Some become sages, learning all they can from tomes and scrolls. Others sit at the feet of the wise, seeking to emulate the elders of their clan or temple. And still others master the persuasive arts, honing their social skills.

Source:	LaserLlama's New & Alternate Player Races v2.0.0 p. 5 (Homebrew)

trait.name: A Diverse People
trait.text:
Humans can vary wildly based on their environment. Where they live, what they do, local climate, their level of education, and other influences all effect their skills and traits. It is hard to make generalizations about humans as the only thing they have in common is their ability to adapt to problems at hand. The wispy and well-educated, scholar from the university of a large city, and the hulking nomadic tribesman from the wilds could share a common relative only two generations back.
	Due to their versatility, humans are capable of conceiving viable offspring with most other mortal races. Unlike elves, dwarves, and orcs, humans are accepting of any half-human that is willing to work together towards the common good.

trait.name: Improvise, Adapt, and Overcome
trait.text:
When a human puts their mind to a task, there is nothing that can stop them. Due to their relatively short lifespans, humans are consumed by an intense desire to leave a unique mark on the world that will live on far past their own demise.
	When combined with their natural talents, this drive allows humans to rival the arcane ability of elvish mages, the martial prowess of orcish warriors, and the craft of dwarven artisans. There is nothing that can hold a dedicated human back from becoming the best there is in their chosen area of mastery.

trait.name: Human Names
trait.text: Humans names, like their other traits, depend on where they live and work. Humans are known for borrowing names from other cultures and races that they work and live closely with.

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: You increase you Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 2, and one other Ability Score of your choice by 1. You cannot select the same Ability Score for both increases you gain from this feature.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Humans reach adulthood in their late teens and can live to see anywhere from seventy to one-hundred years.

trait.name: Alignment
trait.text: Humans tend toward no particular alignment. The best and worst are found among every human culture.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Humans vary in size, from barely 5 feet to well over 6 feet tall. Regardless of your height, your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Determination
trait.text: When you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw without advantage, you can give yourself advantage on that roll. Once you do so, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use this feature again.

trait.name: Sharp Mind
trait.text: You gain proficiency in one Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma-based skill of your choice. When you make an ability check with the proficiency you gain from this feature, you add double your proficiency bonus to your roll.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write both Common and one other language of your choice. Humans often learn the language of other peoples they live and work with.
