trait.name: Rampage
trait.text: When you score a critical hit with a melee attack on your turn, you can move up to half your speed and make a Bite attack as a bonus action.

trait.name: Defiant
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or remove the Frightened or Charmed condition.

trait.name: Tenacity
trait.text: When you finish a short or long rest, you regain additional hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Goblins are small, resourceful fey creatures known for their cunning, tenacity, and boundless energy. Though many associate them with mischief and trickery, goblins are survivors at heart, thriving in the wild, in cities, and in the unpredictable courts of the Feywild. Their fey heritage grants them an uncanny resilience against fear, while their natural agility and ferocity make them dangerous foes despite their small stature. Whether as sneaky rogues, cunning spellcasters, or fearless warriors, goblins bring a mix of scrappy ingenuity and raw determination to any challenge.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Fey

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Small

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Stealth

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition on yourself.

trait.name: Nimble Escape
trait.text: You can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of your turns.

trait.name: Fury of the Small
trait.text: When you damage a creature that is at least one size category larger than you with an attack or a spell, you can deal extra damage equal to your character level. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish long rest.

trait.name: Small Goblin Energy
trait.text: Once per round, when you hit a creature that is at least one size category larger than you with an attack or a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, you deal extra damage equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down, minimum of 1). However, you can only benefit from this trait while Fury of the Small is still available.

trait.name: Bloodied Fury
trait.text: The first time you gain the Bloodied condition in a combat encounter, you can use your reaction to make a single melee attack against a creature within 5 feet of you that is at least one size category larger than you. If you hit, you deal the weapon's normal damage plus extra damage equal to your character level.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Cragmaw Goblins are a savage and twisted variant of their kin, native to the Sword Coast. Their exposure to a fragment of a Netherese obelisk has left them permanently altered, warping their minds and bodies. They bear a more menacing, bestial appearance with jagged teeth, glowing eyes, and an unsettling aura that unnerves even seasoned warriors. This exposure has granted them unnatural resilience and latent psionic energy, making them both cunning and terrifying foes. Though they still possess the goblin drive for survival, their altered nature makes them more aggressive, unpredictable, and prone to violent outbursts.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Fey

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Small

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft.

trait.name: Resistances
trait.text: Psychic

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Arcana

trait.name: Nimble Escape
trait.text: You can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of your turns.

trait.name: Fury of the Small
trait.text: When you damage a creature that is at least one size category larger than you with an attack or a spell, you can deal extra Psychic damage equal to your character level. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Small Goblin Energy
trait.text: Once per round, when you hit a creature that is at least one size category larger than you with an attack or a spell that requires an attack roll, you deal extra Psychic damage equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down, minimum of 1). However, you can only benefit from this trait while Fury of the Small is still available.

trait.name: Toothy Grin
trait.text: As a bonus action, you flash a menacing, unnatural grin at a creature within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become Frightened of you for 1 minute. The DC for this saving throw is equal to your passive Intimidation score (10 + your Intimidation modifier). The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Hobgoblins are disciplined warriors with a deep connection to the Feywild, their ancient homeland. Though they have long since established themselves in the Material Plane, remnants of their fey ancestry linger in their culture and magic. Their societies are built on strict hierarchies, where honor, strategy, and unity are valued above all else. Hobgoblins thrive in structured environments, whether as mercenaries, soldiers, or adventurers, and they possess an innate ability to uplift their allies in times of need.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Fey

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Persuasion

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition on yourself.

trait.name: Fey Gift
trait.text:
You can take the Help action as a bonus action. Additionally, once per long rest, when you use Fey Gift to help an ally, you can choose one of the following benefits to occur alongside the Help action:

	• Hospitality. You and the target each gain temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your proficiency bonus.

	• Passage. You and the target each increase your walking speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

	• Spite. The next time the target hits a creature with an attack, the creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of its next turn.

At 3rd level, whenever you roll initiative, you regain all expended uses of this ability.

trait.name: Fortune of Many
trait.text:
Once per turn, when you make a d20 test, you can gain a bonus to the roll equal to the number of allies within 10 feet of you (maximum bonus of +3).
	You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Koalinths are the disciplined, amphibious kin of hobgoblins, adapted to life beneath the waves. Once exiled from their land-dwelling brethren, they forged their own empire in the depths of the sea, where their rigid martial traditions remain unchanged. Skilled warriors and tactical thinkers, Koalinths command the tides with the same calculated precision as their terrestrial cousins, making them formidable foes and invaluable allies in naval warfare.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Fey

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft., swim 30 ft.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Acrobatics

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Goblin, Primordial (Aquan)

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: You can breathe both air and water.

trait.name: Martial Training
trait.text: You gain proficiency with all martial weapons.

trait.name: Martial Advantage
trait.text: Once per turn, when you have advantage on a weapon or spell attack roll that deals damage, you deal additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus on a hit.

trait.name: Fortune of Many
trait.text:
Once per turn, when you make a d20 test, you can gain a bonus to the roll equal to the number of allies within 10 feet of you (maximum bonus of +3).
	You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Long ago, the Kenku soared the skies, their wings carrying them across vast landscapes while their voices wove enchanting songs. But their hubris angered a powerful being, who struck them with a terrible curse—stealing their wings and warping their voices. Now, while Kenku can still speak clearly, most instinctively communicate through mimicry, repeating the voices and sounds they have heard throughout their lives.
	Living in the shadows, many Kenku seek to undo the curse that plagues their species, while others search for magic or inventions that might one day return them to the sky. Clever and resourceful, they use their talents to survive in a world that often sees them as little more than remnants of a forgotten past.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Monstrosity

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: two skills of your choice (Stealth and Performance are recommended)

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Primordial (Auran)

trait.name: Expert Duplication
trait.text: You have an uncanny ability to replicate craftsmanship. You gain the Crafter feat.

trait.name: Kenku Recall
trait.text:
You have the ability to recall details with remarkable clarity.

	• Recall Lore. When you make an Intelligence check to recall information, you can give yourself advantage on the roll. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

	• Practiced Hand. Once per day, when you make a skill check with one of the two skills you chose when making your Kenku, you can give yourself expertise in that skill for that roll (adding twice your proficiency bonus).

trait.name: Mimicry
trait.text: You can mimic sounds and voices you have heard. A creature that hears the sounds you make can tell they are imitations with a Wisdom (Insight) check against your passive Deception (10 + your deception modifier).

trait.name: Cursed
trait.text: Because you already live with a life-altering curse, you have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the effects of other Curses.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Kobolds are small, cunning, and deeply tied to dragons, believing themselves to be distant kin to these mighty creatures. While often underestimated, their ingenuity, resilience, and natural affinity for magic make them far more capable than their size suggests. Many kobolds revere dragons as deities, while others seek to carve out their own legends, proving their worth through intellect, craftiness, or sheer determination.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Dragon

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Small

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiency
trait.text: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Sleight of Hand, or Survival.

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Draconic, Undercommon

trait.name: Draconic Cry
trait.text:
As a bonus action, you let out a piercing cry that unsettles your foes. Until the start of your next turn, allies have advantage on attack rolls against any enemies within 10 feet of you that can hear you.
	You can use this trait once, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest. Additionally you regain all expended uses whenever you roll for initiative.

trait.name: Defiance
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition.

trait.name: Draconic Sorcery
trait.text:
You have a spark of draconic magic within you. When you create your kobold you learn one cantrip of your choice from the following list:

	• Fire Bolt
	• Ray of Frost
	• Thunderclap

You always have this cantrip prepared. When you cast a spell using this trait, you choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability (choose the ability when you create your Kobold).

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Kobolds are small, cunning, and deeply tied to dragons, believing themselves to be distant kin to these mighty creatures. While often underestimated, their ingenuity, resilience, and natural affinity for magic make them far more capable than their size suggests. Many kobolds revere dragons as deities, while others seek to carve out their own legends, proving their worth through intellect, craftiness, or sheer determination.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.text: Small

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft. fly 30 ft. (See Flight)

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiency
trait.text: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Sleight of Hand, or Survival.

trait.name: Flight
trait.text: You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.

trait.name: Draconic Cry
trait.text:
As a bonus action, you let out a piercing cry that unsettles your foes. Until the start of your next turn, allies have advantage on attack rolls against any enemies within 10 feet of you that can hear you.
	You can use this trait once, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest. Additionally you regain all expended uses whenever you roll for initiative.

trait.name: Defiance
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
The Kuo-Toa are a twisted, aquatic people warped by centuries of madness and exposure to their own insecurities. Once a peaceful coastal species, they claim to be the remnants of a powerful undersea empire that was betrayed and destroyed by surface-dwelling species. While no records of such an empire exist outside Kuo-Toa myths, they fiercely cling to this belief. Whether rooted in truth or delusion, this paranoia fuels their deep mistrust of land-dwellers. Many Kuo-Toa view outsiders as agents of the surface conspiracy and are quick to react with hostility or suspicion.
	Despite their fractured minds, Kuo-Toa possess a unique awareness of otherworldly entities, and some are even known to create false deities through sheer belief.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Aberration

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft., swim 30 ft.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiency
trait.text: Religion

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Undercommon, Primordial (Aquan)

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: You can breathe both air and water.

trait.name: Otherworldly Perception
trait.text: As a bonus action, you can heighten your awareness to gain truesight out to a range of 30 feet for 1 minute. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Slippery
trait.text: You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or remove the Grappled condition.

trait.name: Sunlight Anathema
trait.text: The light of the sun disorients you. While in direct sunlight, you cannot add your Dexterity modifier to your Armor Class (if applicable).

trait.name: Net Master
trait.text:
You have learned to wield nets with deadly precision.

	• When you make an attack with a Net, you add your Strength modifier as well as your Dexterity modifier when calculating the Dexterity saving throw DC to avoid being restrained.
	• The escape DC for a Net you throw is equal to 10 + your Strength modifier.

trait.name: Spurious Blessing
trait.text:
You know the Sacred Flame cantrip. However, when you cast it, the spell deals cold damage instead of radiant.
	You always have this cantrip prepared. When you cast a spell using this trait, you choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability (choose the ability when you create your Kuo-Toa).

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Born from the union of the Material Plane and the Elemental Plane of Earth, Lizardfolk are hardy, stoic beings shaped by their elemental heritage. These reptilian people are pragmatic survivors, viewing the world through a lens of practicality rather than emotion. Their connection to stone and soil is deeply ingrained, allowing them to instinctively manipulate earth magic to shape their surroundings.
	Lizardfolk often dwell in coastal marshes, rocky riverbeds, and dense jungles, where their natural resilience and elemental attunement give them an advantage. While they rarely seek conflict, their calm detachment can make them seem cold or unfeeling to outsiders.
	Though Lizardfolk are not inherently hostile, they are fiercely territorial and will defend their homes with ruthless efficiency.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Elemental

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Small or Medium (2-3 feet or 4-6 feet)

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft., swim 15 ft., burrow 15 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Nature

trait.name: Bite
trait.text: Unarmed strikes made with your fanged maw deal 1d6 Piercing damage instead of the normal Bludgeoning damage. This is a Strength-based attack, and you are proficient with it. If you score a critical hit with this attack, you gain temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.

trait.name: Natural Armor
trait.text: Your scales provide ample protection. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

trait.name: Geomancy
trait.text:
Your affinity with the Elemental Plane of Earth grants you certain magical gifts:

	• You know the Elementalism cantrip, which you can cast at will.

	• At 5th level, you learn Spike Growth. You always have these spells prepared.

You can cast each of them once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. When you cast a spell using this trait, you choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability (choose the ability when you create your Lizardfolk).

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Minotaurs are formidable beings shaped by their labyrinthine heritage and the twisted influence of Baphomet, the Horned King. Towering over most humanoids, they possess the strength of a bull and a mind sharpened by primal instinct. Minotaurs are often found in sprawling labyrinths, serving as both hunters and guardians.
	Despite their imposing nature, Minotaurs are not inherently violent. Many live by a strict code of honor, blending their strength with strategy. However, whispers of Baphomet's influence linger within their culture, offering dark boons to those who embrace his chaotic power.
	Minotaurs are natural pathfinders, their uncanny sense of direction making them excellent trackers and survivalists.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Playing a Minotaur
trait.text:
While Minotaurs trace their lineage back to the Abyss and the demon lord Baphomet, the Minotaurs found on the Material Plane are a divergent subspecies. These Minotaurs have lived far from the influence of their Abyssal cousins, forging their own path in the mortal world.
	Unlike the brutal, bloodthirsty Minotaurs of the Abyss, Material Plane Minotaurs are smaller in stature and more adaptable in temperament. While still proud and fiercely independent, they are typically more welcoming of outsiders and willing to form bonds with other societies.
	Many Minotaurs struggle with the dark whispers of their heritage, but they often channel this inner turmoil into strength, embracing discipline and personal codes of honor to resist Baphomet's influence. As a Minotaur adventurer, you embody this balance — a formidable warrior shaped by tradition, yet free to forge your own destiny.

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Monstrosity

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium (5-7 feet)

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Survival

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Abyssal, Minotaur

trait.name: Horns
trait.text:
Your horns are a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal 1d6 + your Strength modifier piercing damage instead of the normal bludgeoning damage.
	Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with your horns, you can push the target 10 feet away from you.

trait.name: Goring Rush
trait.text: When you take the Dash action on your turn, you can make one melee attack with your horns as part of the same action.

trait.name: Baphomet's Blessing
trait.text:
The chaotic power of Baphomet lingers in your blood, manifesting in various gifts. At 1st level, choose one of the following traits. You gain a second trait from this list once you reach 5th level.

	Grievous Strike. When you score a critical hit with your horns, you deal an additional 1d8 piercing damage.

	Sure-Footed. Non-magical difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement.

	Baphomet's Favor. When you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you can use your reaction to reroll the attack roll. You must use the second roll. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

	Abyssal Resilience. When you are forced to make a saving throw against a spell or effect that deals psychic or necrotic damage, you can roll a d4 and add the result to your saving throw.

	Raging Fury. When you gain the bloodied condition for the first time in an encounter, you have advantage on the next attack roll you make on your next turn. If you hit with this attack, you deal additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Satyrs are lively and mischievous fey creatures, known for their boundless energy, love of revelry, and irresistible charm. Standing between 3 and 5 feet tall, they possess the legs and horns of a goat and an unshakable zest for life. Though often seen as carefree wanderers, Satyrs are deeply connected to the Feywild and its magic, granting them a natural resistance to enchantment and illusion.
	Whether playing enchanting melodies, dancing through combat, or weaving magic into their movements, Satyrs bring joy and chaos in equal measure. Their natural charisma makes them skilled performers and persuasive speakers, but their fey nature ensures they remain unpredictable.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Fey

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Medium (3-5 feet tall)

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 35 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiencies
trait.text: Performance, Persuasion

trait.name: Ram
trait.text: Your head and horns are a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal 1d6 + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Fey Resistance
trait.text: You have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Fey Melody
trait.text:
You perform an enchanting song that targets a creature of your choice within 60 feet. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC = 10 + your Performance bonus) or be affected by one of the following conditions (your choice when you use this ability):

	• Charming. The target gains the Charmed and Incapacitated conditions until the end of your next turn and must use all its movement to move toward you.

	• Frightening. The target gains the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions and must use all its movement to safely move as far away from you as possible.

Once you use this trait, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Mirthful Movement
trait.text:
You can cast Jump and Longstrider (with a duration of 1 minute).
	You always have these spells prepared. You can cast each of them at will without expending a spell slot, only targeting yourself when you do so. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level, targeting creatures other than yourself.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Few undead possess true sapience, and intelligent skeletons are among the rarest of their kind. Some originate from the necropolis of Evernight in the Shadowfell, a city of the dead where ancient magics sustain them. However, most are the discarded remnants of powerful spellcasters—animated to serve, only to be abandoned when their usefulness wanes. Despite their unnatural existence, some skeletons retain a flicker of free will, forging their own paths in a world that often fears them.
	Devoid of flesh and incapable of speech, skeletons rely on the residual necromantic energy that sustains them. Their brittle bones make them fragile in battle, but their undead nature grants them unnatural resilience and a lingering connection to the magic that first reanimated them.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Undead

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Small or Medium

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiency
trait.text: History

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Any (see Limited Telepathy)

trait.name: Vulnerability
trait.text: Bludgeoning (see Brittle Bones)

trait.name: Resistances
trait.text: Poison

trait.name: Blindsight
trait.text: 90 ft. (blind beyond this range).

trait.name: Brittle Bones
trait.text: Your skeletal form makes you vulnerable to crushing blows. You have vulnerability to bludgeoning damage unless you are wearing heavy armor.

trait.name: Limited Telepathy
trait.text: You cannot speak, but you can communicate telepathically with creatures within 90 feet. This communication is one-way; you can send thoughts, but you cannot receive them telepathically.

trait.name: Residual Necromancy
trait.text:
The magic that binds your soul to your bones grants you a lingering connection to necrotic forces. When you create your skeleton, choose one cantrip from the following list:

	• Chill Touch
	• Poison Spray
	• Toll the Dead.

You always have this cantrip prepared. When casting a spell using this trait, choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability (this choice is made when you create your skeleton).

trait.name: Spark of Life
trait.text: Though undead, the magic that reanimated you carries a flicker of vitality. You regain hit points from spells, potions, and resting as though you were a living creature.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Thri-Kreen are insectoid nomads, bound by a deep connection to their clutch—the small group they hatch and grow alongside. While individualistic in nature, they retain strong communal instincts, often perceiving their allies as an extension of their own clutch. Their alien physiology grants them unique advantages, including natural camouflage, additional limbs, and the ability to communicate telepathically with those who do not understand their spoken language.
	Though they are skilled hunters and survivalists, Thri-Kreen possess a rich oral history passed down through generations. Their clutches share knowledge instinctively, leading them to recall ancient lore as if it were their own lived experience.

Source:	Sewage Orc

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: Monstrosity

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Small or Medium

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: 30 ft.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: 60 ft.

trait.name: Skill Proficiency
trait.text: History

trait.name: Suggested Languages
trait.text: Thri-Kreen (see Limited Telepathy)

trait.name: Chameleon Carapace
trait.text: While you aren't wearing armor, your carapace gives you a base Armor Class of 13 + your Dexterity modifier. As an action, you can change the color of your carapace to match the color and texture of your surroundings, giving you advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in those surroundings. Additionally, until you move, or take the Attack or Spell Attack action, directly after you have changed your carapace, you can attempt the hide action as if you were heavily obscured.

trait.name: Secondary Arms
trait.text: You have two slightly smaller secondary arms below your primary pair. These secondary arms can manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down a Tiny object, or wield a weapon with the light property. You only gain the benefits of a weapon's mastery property (if applicable) if the weapon is wielded in one of your primary arms.

trait.name: Limited Telepathy
trait.text: You can only speak the Thri-Kreen language aloud, but you can communicate telepathically in any other languages you know with creatures within 90 feet. This communication is one-way; you can send thoughts, but you cannot receive them telepathically.

trait.name: Clutch Recall
trait.text: The shared knowledge of your clutch lingers in your mind, allowing you to instinctively recall important information. You can automatically succeed on a History check to recall knowledge. Once you use this trait, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

fields.name: Actor
fields.text:
Skilled at mimicry and dramatics, you gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks when trying to pass yourself off as a different person.

	• You can mimic the speech of another person or the sounds made by other creatures. You must have heard the person speaking, or heard the creature make the sound, for at least 1 minute. A successful Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check allows a listener to determine that the effect is faked.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Alert
fields.text:
Always on the lookout for danger, you gain the following benefits:

	• You gain a +5 bonus to initiative.

	• You can't be surprised while you are conscious.

	• Other creatures don't gain advantage on attack rolls against you as a result of being unseen by you.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Athlete (Dexterity)
fields.text:
You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• When you are prone, standing up uses only 5 feet of your movement.

	• Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement.

	• You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10 feet.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Athlete (Strength)
fields.text:
You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• When you are prone, standing up uses only 5 feet of your movement.

	• Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement.

	• You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10 feet.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Charger
fields.text:
When you use your action to Dash, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to shove a creature.
	If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Crossbow Expert
fields.text:
Thanks to extensive practice with the crossbow, you gain the following benefits:

	• You ignore the loading quality of crossbows with which you are proficient.

	• Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

	• When you use the Attack action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a hand crossbow you are holding.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Defensive Duelist
fields.text:
When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Dual Wielder
fields.text:
You master fighting with two weapons, gaining the following benefits:

	• You gain a +1 bonus to AC while you are wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand.

	• You can use two-weapon fighting even when the one-handed melee weapons you are wielding aren't light.

	• You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 165

fields.name: Dungeon Delver
fields.text:
Alert to the hidden traps and secret doors found in many dungeons, you gain the following benefits:

	• You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to detect the presence of secret doors.

	• You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid or resist traps.

	• You have resistance to the damage dealt by traps.

	• Traveling at a fast pace doesn't impose the normal -5 penalty on your passive Wisdom (Perception) score.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 166

fields.name: Durable
fields.text:
Hardy and resilient, you gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, the minimum number of hit points you regain from the roll equals twice your Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 166

fields.name: Elemental Adept (Acid)
fields.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell
fields.text:
When you gain this feat, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
	Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll damage for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2.
	You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 166

fields.name: Grappler
fields.text:
You've developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close-quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits:

	• You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature you are grappling.

	• You can use your action to try to pin a creature grappled by you. To do so, make another grapple check. If you succeed, you and the creature are both restrained until the grapple ends.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Great Weapon Master
fields.text:
You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits:

	• On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action.

	• Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Healer
fields.text:
You are an able physician, allowing you to mend wounds quickly and get your allies back in the fight. You gain the following benefits:

	• When you use a healer's kit to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 hit point.

	• As an action, you can spend one use of a healer's kit to tend to a creature and restore 1d6 + 4 hit points to it, plus additional hit points equal to the creature's maximum number of Hit Dice. The creature can't regain hit points from this feat again until it finishes a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Heavily Armored
fields.text:
You have trained to master the use of heavy armor, gaining the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Heavy Armor Master
fields.text:
You can use your armor to deflect strikes that would kill others. You gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• While you are wearing heavy armor, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical weapons is reduced by 3.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Inspiring Leader
fields.text:
You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Keen Mind
fields.text:
You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision. You gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You always know which way is north.

	• You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.

	• You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Lightly Armored (Dexterity)
fields.text:
You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You gain proficiency with light armor.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Lightly Armored (Strength)
fields.text:
You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You gain proficiency with light armor.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Linguist
fields.text:
You have studied languages and codes, gaining the following benefits:

	• Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You learn three languages of your choice.

	• You can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Lucky
fields.text:
You have inexplicable luck that seems to kick in at just the right moment.
	You have 3 luck points. Whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can spend one luck point to roll an additional d20. You can choose to spend one of your luck points after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You choose which of the d20s is used for the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.
	You can also spend one luck point when an attack roll is made against you. Roll a d20, and then choose whether the attack uses the attacker's roll or yours. If more than one creature spends a luck point to influence the outcome of a roll, the points cancel each other out; no additional dice are rolled.
	You regain your expended luck points when you finish a long rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 167

fields.name: Mage Slayer
fields.text:
You have practiced techniques useful in melee combat against spellcasters, gaining the following benefits:

	• When a creature within 5 feet of you casts a spell, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

	• When you damage a creature that is concentrating on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain its concentration.

	• You have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creatures within 5 feet of you.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Magic Initiate (Bard)
fields.text:
You learn two bard cantrips of your choice.
	In addition, choose one 1st-level bard spell. You learn that spell and can cast it at its lowest level. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
	Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Magic Initiate (Cleric)
fields.text:
You learn two cleric cantrips of your choice.
	In addition, choose one 1st-level cleric spell. You learn that spell and can cast it at its lowest level. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
	Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Wisdom.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

	In addition, choose one 1st-level druid spell. You learn that spell and can cast it at its lowest level. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
	Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Wisdom.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

	In addition, choose one 1st-level sorcerer spell. You learn that spell and can cast it at its lowest level. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
	Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

	In addition, choose one 1st-level warlock spell. You learn that spell and can cast it at its lowest level. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
	Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.text:

	In addition, choose one 1st-level wizard spell. You learn that spell and can cast it at its lowest level. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
	Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Martial Adept
fields.text:
You have martial training that allows you to perform special combat maneuvers. You gain the following benefits:

	• You learn two maneuvers of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype in the fighter class (Added as spells in the Maneuvers spell list). If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

	• You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Medium Armor Master
fields.text:
You have practiced moving in medium armor to gain the following benefits:

	• Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

	• When you wear medium armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Mobile
fields.text:
You are exceptionally speedy and agile. You gain the following benefits:

	• Your speed increases by 10 feet.

	• When you use the Dash action, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement on that turn.

	• When you make a melee attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or not.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Moderately Armored (Dexterity)
fields.text:
You have trained to master the use of medium armor and shields, gaining the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Moderately Armored (Strength)
fields.text:

	• You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Mounted Combatant
fields.text:
You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted. While you are mounted and aren't incapacitated, you gain the following benefits:

	• You have advantage on melee attack rolls against any unmounted creature that is smaller than your mount.

	• You can force an attack targeted at your mount to target you instead.

	• If your mount is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Observant (Intelligence)
fields.text:
Quick to notice details of your environment, you gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• If you can see a creature's mouth while it is speaking a language you understand, you can interpret what it's saying by reading its lips.

	• You have a +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Observant (Wisdom)
fields.text:

	• Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You have a +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Polearm Master
fields.text:
You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons. You gain the following benefits:

	• When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon's damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage.

	• While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, quarterstaff, or spear, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter your reach.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Resilient (Charisma)
fields.text:
Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits:

	• Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.text:

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 168

fields.name: Ritual Caster (Bard)
fields.text:
You have learned a number of spells that you can cast as rituals. These spells are written in a ritual book, which you must have in hand while casting one of them.
	When you choose this feat, you acquire a ritual book holding two 1st-level bard spells of your choice. The spells you choose must have the ritual tag. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
	If you come across a spell in written form, such as a magical spell scroll or a wizard's spellbook, you might be able to add it to your ritual book. The spell must be on the bard spell list, the spell's level can be no higher than half your level (rounded up), and it must have the ritual tag. The process of copying the spell into your ritual book takes 2 hours per level of the spell, and costs 50 gp per level. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 169

fields.name: Savage Attacker
fields.text:
Once per turn when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 169

fields.name: Sentinel
fields.text:
You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits:

	• When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.

	• Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action before leaving your reach.

	• When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 169

fields.name: Sharpshooter
fields.text:
You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits:

	• Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.

	• Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.

	• Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Shield Master
fields.text:
You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a shield:

	• If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to shove a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield.

	• If you aren't incapacitated, you can add your shield's AC bonus to any Dexterity saving throw you make against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you.

	• If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Skilled
fields.text:
You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Skulker
fields.text:
You are expert at slinking through shadows. You gain the following benefits:

	• You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding.

	• When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.

	• Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Spell Sniper
fields.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell
fields.text:
You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits:

	• When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled.

	• Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.

	• You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll. Choose the cantrip from the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the spell list you chose from: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Tavern Brawler (Constitution)
fields.text:
Accustomed to rough-and-tumble fighting using whatever weapons happen to be at hand, you gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You are proficient with improvised weapons.

	• Your unarmed strike uses a d4 for damage.

	• When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Tavern Brawler (Strength)
fields.text:

	• You are proficient with improvised weapons.

	• Your unarmed strike uses a d4 for damage.

	• When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Tough
fields.text:
Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a level thereafter, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: War Caster
fields.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell
fields.text:
You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

	• You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell when you take damage.

	• You can perform the somatic components of spells even when you have weapons or a shield in one or both hands.

	• When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to cast a spell at the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack. The spell must have a casting time of 1 action and must target only that creature.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Weapon Master (Dexterity)
fields.text:
You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice. Each one must be a simple or a martial weapon.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 170

fields.name: Fighting Style: Archery
fields.text:
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 72

fields.name: Fighting Style: Defense
fields.text:
While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 72

fields.name: Fighting Style: Dueling
fields.text:
When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 72

fields.name: Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting
fields.text:
When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 72

fields.name: Fighting Style: Protection
fields.text:
When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 72

fields.name: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting
fields.text:
When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 72

fields.name: Bountiful Luck
fields.text:
Your people have extraordinary luck, which you have learned to mystically lend to your companions when you see them falter. You're not sure how you do it; you just wish it, and it happens. Surely a sign of fortune's favor!
	When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you rolls a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to let the ally reroll the die. The ally must use the new roll.
	When you use this ability, you can't use your Lucky racial trait before the end of your next turn.

Source:	Xanathar's Guide to Everything p. 73

fields.name: Dragon Fear (Charisma)
fields.text:
When angered, you radiate menace. You gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Constitution or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• Instead of exhaling destructive energy, you can expend a use of your Breath Weapon trait to roar, forcing each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). A target automatically succeeds on the save if it can't hear or see you. On a failed save, a target becomes frightened of you for 1 minute. If the frightened target takes any damage, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Frightened:
	• A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight.
	• The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.

Source:	Xanathar's Guide to Everything p. 74

fields.name: Dragon Hide (Charisma)
fields.text:
You manifest scales and claws reminiscent of your draconic ancestors. You gain the following benefits:

	• Increase your Strength or Constitution or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

	• Your scales harden. While you aren't wearing armor, you can calculate your AC as 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

	• You grow retractable claws from the tips of your fingers. Extending or retracting the claws requires no action. The claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes.
